These are the only player rows of 2019-2021 (2,732 of 2,740 equal on eight counts by my own link and parse) whose RG record differs from Sackmann's. No decided correction names these rows; the candidate applies them and they read exchanged afterwards.

W22.reasons: The rule applies. Feed held: I parsed 3,768 RG statistics documents (2019-2026; the 56 absent codes are the 96-player women's qualifying of 2019-2020) and decrypted 3,740 MatchBeats documents (2019-2026); key statistics for 2025-2026. Matched Sackmann's history: 2,732 of 2,740 player rows of 2019-2021 equal on all eight counts, the other 8 being the RGX boxes; TML's men's RG rows of 2019-2021 also equal RG on every count. From 2022 Sackmann's RG rows come from another record: TML's men's main-draw rows of 2022-2025 copy his values (first serves in equal to the row in 97-100% of rows), its qualifying rows copy RG's (98.6-100%), and SofaScore shares his (round 1). Applying the rule to his own 2022-2025 history is justified on the data because the rule's reason holds more strongly here than at Wimbledon and the US Open: RG's statistics are exactly what the training data measured for RG until 2021. It extends the decision's scope (6 Oct applied it to 2026 rows and left this study to measure RG 2022-2025), so accepting it stays the owner's call through the candidate build. Why the source rule rather than the 8 Oct bar: on the small differences the 8 Oct bar would keep, the independent records side with RG as they do on the large ones. Whole split (round 1's test), every refereed row BEFORE the lead's referee exclusion: RG closer on 368, the row on 5, 3 ties (376 rows); first serves in differing by at most one: 149 against 4; sign '-' 33 against 2; sign '0' 12 against 0. Other counts on the proposed matches, valid referees only: aces 14 RG / 0 row, double faults 25/0, serve points 106/0 (60/0 where the row has more points, 46/0 where fewer), break points faced 11/0 and saved 10/0, service games 22/0; the referees' calibrated accuracy on undisputed rows makes 4 row-closer readings out of 153 one-point differences consistent with chart noise. The differences are not symmetric noise: aces are lower in the row on 81 of 83 changing rows (65 by one), double faults on 182 of 203 (142 by one), and where the row has more serve points RG's own point-by-point equals RG's statistics on 191 of 192. So the expected error of taking RG's value is a few percent and of keeping the row's the rest. With the candidate, every edition's pooled first-serve-in rate equals RG's own (men's qualifying 68.5/65.3/65.2/68.6% become 62.5/61.5/61.5/63.4%, against 61.3-62.7% in 2019-2021), aces and double faults per serve point rise to RG's level, and hold rates and serve points per game do not move. Departure from round 1: under the 8 Oct bar I dropped 'both-minus' sides (both players with fewer first serves in from Sackmann); under the source rule I keep them. In that pattern the referees read RG on 4 of 6 refereed rows, the 2 contrary readings (Van de Zandschulp by Court Vision, contradicted by the hand chart; Arnaboldi by a hand chart alone) are in matches the lead already excludes, nothing contradicts RG on the remaining both-minus matches, and the stakes are 1-3 first serves in. Service games: in completed matches MatchBeats' count fits the score exactly where the row's does not (e.g. Djokovic-Fucsovics, Muchova-Sabalenka); in 8 W22 retirements MatchBeats counts the unfinished game (+1) where Sackmann's rows never do; both pass B5 and Court Vision and the charts count like MatchBeats, so I accept it. The fallback (the row's own count, 20 matches whose MatchBeats lacks points or is absent) is acceptable: it fits the score and equals MatchBeats where MatchBeats holds the games; it is the one count not from RG's record.

W26.reasons: This is the 6 Oct rule as decided for Wimbledon and the US Open 2026: rows after Sackmann's end, the Slam's feed held and matched to his history; the 8 Oct bar has no meaning for blank rows. Main draws: nothing in Sackmann's blank rows is replaced; RG's record of each match is linked by names and round, its sets equal the row's score (retirements apart, where RG adds a 0-0 set) and its winner the row's winner. RG's record is internally consistent: its statistics equal MatchBeats and the key statistics on every complete player row (663 of the 664 rows are complete). The 2026 hand charts (23 women's main-draw matches, 46 rows; 1 men's qualifying match) read RG's values at or above their calibrated accuracy: serve points 98%, aces 96%, double faults 100%, first serves in 92%, points won on each serve 98%, break points and service games 100% (calibration 2019-2021: 90, 91, 99, 79, 90, 100, 100%). TML's men's main-draw rows of 2026, which Stage 0 does not use, carry the first-serve fault (first serves in equal to RG on 44% of rows; pooled 64.7% against RG's 62.2%), so RG is the only clean record. Qualifying: TML writes 0 service games in 194 of 224 player rows, break points saved above faced in 12 matches and partial boxes in 3 (Stage 0 drops those 14 boxes, B4 and B9), and serve points equal to RG's in only 69% of rows; its pooled first-serve rate is level with RG's (63.2% against 63.1%), so this is not the first-serve fault but a noisier record, which the rule replaces as it replaced TML's Wimbledon and US Open 2026 rows even where they agreed. With the candidate: 251 blank, 14 failed-check and 62 service-games-missing rows of 2026 hold a full box; pooled first serves in 62.2% (men's main) and 63.0% (women's main), inside RG's 2019-2025 range.

other_findings: 1. TML's Roland-Garros men's rows are copies, not a referee: in 2022-2025 the main-draw rows carry Sackmann's values (first serves in equal to his row in 97-100% of rows, to RG's in 42-82%) and the qualifying rows carry RG's (98.6-100%); in 2019-2021 all three records agree. So Sackmann's main-draw fault is in the record TML also reads, while his qualifying comes from yet another record. 2. Scope gap (not an error; addressed by the amended proposal, see the addendum): 22 matches the lead classes 'equal' (18 of RG 2026 qualifying, where TML writes 0 service games, and 4 of 2023) keep missing or B5-failing service games although MatchBeats holds them complete and fitting the score; under the same rule they could take MatchBeats' service games with nothing else changing. In 15 more 'equal' matches the row's usable service games differ from MatchBeats' (both fitting the score). 3. Retirement convention (addressed by the amended proposal, see the addendum): in 11 confirmed matches (8 W22, 3 W26) MatchBeats counts the game in progress at the retirement as a service game (sum one above the score's games); Sackmann's RG rows never do (2019-2025); both pass B5 and Court Vision and the charts count like MatchBeats (rolandgarros:2022/QM041, 2022/SM038, 2023/QM117, 2024/QM044, 2024/SM038, 2025/SM115, 2026/SM084, 2026/SM077, 2022/SD073, 2023/SD081, 2026/SD062). 4. The lead's referee exclusion is conservative: on the whole split RG's record is closer on 19 of the 26 refereed rows of the 13 excluded matches (row 5, ties 2); several exclusions rest on one hand-chart first-serve count that the same chart's points won contradict (Seyboth Wild, Alcaraz 2025 QF, Ruud 2025 R128, Djokovic 2023 R64). Djokovic-Fucsovics 2023 R64 also keeps the row's service games (9 and 9 for 27 games, failing B5) while Court Vision and the chart read MatchBeats' 13 and 14. Not proposed, so not voted. 5. Court Vision 2023-2024 is a usable referee for serve points, aces, service games and break points (exact on 95-100% of undisputed rows), though not for double faults (40-64%) or the split (first serves in 25-62%). 6. My round-1 exclusion of Pigossi-Kawa (2024 Q2) is resolved: the whole box from RG replaces both sides, and the match passes every check with it. The extreme partial boxes (Barrios Vera-Kovalik, Uchijima-Yuan, Salkova-Serban, Tikhonova-Fourlis, the 2026 TML partial rows) return with RG's complete boxes. 7. The lead's figures I recomputed hold: E1 (2,732/2,740), E2 (Court Vision 2022 first serves in 232/0/236, hand charts 130/0/140, aces 81 of 83 lower in the row with 65 by one; double faults 182 lower of 203 changing where the row has a value, the lead's 207 includes 4 blank values), E4 (194/224 zeros; 15 matches without a box), E6 (3,265 rows, 0 outside, 252 boxes given), E7 (classes). 8. The one equal-class match the amended proposal leaves out (Baez d. Heide, RG 2024 R128, mb_contradicts): RG's statistics and MatchBeats differ by one point on Heide's first-serve points won (40 against 39), a count the override would leave as it is; only Baez's service games would change (22 to 23: the row's 22 and 22 make 44 in a 45-game match without a tiebreak, and MatchBeats and the alternation give 23 and 22). It could be in on the service games alone; not proposed, so not voted. 10. SVX: the Court Vision copy flags the games after 6-6 of an advantage final set (RG until 2021) as tiebreak games, so counting service games by its is_tiebreak flag undercounts long final sets (Wawrinka d. Tsitsipas 8-6, Rodionov d. Chardy 10-8 and 7 matches whose row is right); count a game as a tiebreak only where both players serve in it. 11. That is evidence for the undecided 'service-game mismatches that are not exact swaps'; they would take the truth, not an exchange. 12. SVX: the swapped RG 2023 match left out (Diaz Acosta d. Agamenone, Q1) is already corrected by its confirmed override (11 and 10, the truth). 13. SVX: my proof test is stricter than the lead's on two matches the lead classes equal (no gap in game numbers) and looser on one the lead classes unproven; none is a swap, so the proposal does not move. 14. SVX addendum: the proof test should not key a file's games by their numbers alone. The AO 2024 file of Griekspoor d. Safiullin repeats game 4 and mixes servers in game 5 of set 4, and keying by (set, game) merges the repeat so the alternation passes; checking that game numbers run without repeat or gap catches it. Here the independent records settle the match, so nothing changes. 15. SVX addendum: Court Vision's AO copy uses the MatchBeats files' own player ids as server ids, so its first server maps onto the files without names. 16. SVX addendum: the hand charts' 17 first-server mismatches are all on AO qualifying matches with no MatchBeats file (2018-2020, 2022), so there is nothing to compare; on every match with a file they agree. 17. SVX addendum 2: RG 2017's 132 'other' matches all give the two players equal service games; 123 of them carry 0 and 0, which Stage 0 treats as missing (its rule for service games recorded as 0 with serve points played), not a B5 failure; 6 have the right total split equally where the score forces unequal counts; 3 are 8-13 games short. Where the first server is proven, the score's alternation would fill or correct them as the RG 2026 zeros were filled; not proposed, so not voted. 18. SVX addendum 2: my proof test agrees with the lead's new strict flag on RG 2016-2018. AO 2019 MS140, which that flag fails, passes mine: the split set records keep set 3 and run games 9 and 10 on from 8, so my game-sequence check sees no repeat or gap. The chart and Court Vision readings confirm it either way. 19. SVS: the break-point identity is an independent check of the first server, built from Sackmann's break points and not MatchBeats' labels. It rejected the other first server wherever that would change the counts (300 of 300 sets), and among my 810 swaps it failed only for Stosur d. Halep, which I withdraw. 20. SVS: the other sets change values inside Stage 0's B5 tolerance in usable boxes, so they move hold rates without changing box status; only the fills (and one B5 failure, RG 2023) bring boxes back.

addendum.reasons: My own derivation, independent of the lead's code: MatchBeats decrypted and counted as completed, non-tiebreak games per server (isGameComplete is present on every game of every route, 2019-2026, and is false only on the last game of 33 documents: 25 retirements, 3 captures still in progress, and 5 placeholder documents of 2026 walkovers or a match outside Stage 0); and the score's alternation, from the row's score and the player MatchBeats has serving the first point, servers alternating game by game with a tiebreak taking one turn uncounted. The two agree on all 42 matches where MatchBeats holds every point. The other 2 rest on the alternation because their MatchBeats documents are captures that stop before the last game: Maestrelli d. Noguchi 3-6 7-6 6-2 (Noguchi serves first, every game the document holds follows the alternation, and the missing final game is Maestrelli's, hence 14 and 15, summing to the 29 non-tiebreak games) and Molcan d. Crawford 1-6 6-4 6-1 (24 games without a tiebreak: 12 each whoever served first). Retirements: a score holds only finished games, so the alternation gives the completed-games count; MatchBeats flags exactly one unfinished game, the last, served by the player whose count drops; in the 8 W22 retirements the new value equals Sackmann's own count, which in every RG retirement of 2019-2025 leaves the unfinished game out, so those overrides no longer change service games and the convention is the training data's, as for tiebreaks (my round-2 finding 3, now addressed). The added matches: in the 10 of 2023-2024 the row's count is impossible under the score (Muchova d. Podoroska 13 and 11 in 24 games without a tiebreak; Muchova d. Sabalenka 15 and 16 for 36 non-tiebreak games, failing B5; the other 8 one game short of the score), so the row is corrupt and the fix is forced by the score and the first server; the 19 TML zeros and 3 Sackmann blanks are missing values Stage 0 drops today, filled with RG's completed games (my round-2 finding 2, now addressed). Independent records hold 7 of the 44 matches and agree: Court Vision and the charts count games with a point served, so in the 4 retirements they hold (Kalinina, Van de Zandschulp, Noskova, Rinderknech) they read the new value plus the unfinished game for its server, and elsewhere exactly the new values (Day-Avanesyan 17-17, Muchova-Sabalenka 18-18, De Jong-Draper 26-26). SVX.scope: All 323 proposed swaps (swaps_scope.csv): AO 2025 81 (36 men's, 45 women's), RG 2019 71, RG 2020 79, RG 2021 92; exchange_svgms on Sackmann's row. Bar: the 8 Oct bar. Test per match, all from my own code: (1) the first server is proven by the Slam's MatchBeats file under a test stricter than the brief's (first point in set 1 game 1, no gap in set or game numbers, one server for every point of a non-tiebreak game, and every game in file order on the alternation's turn, a tiebreak by its first point); (2) the row's two counts are the truth's two exchanged, and the truth's two differ (the truth: the row's score read from that first server, servers alternating game by game, a tiebreak taking one turn uncounted, a retirement's unfinished game not in the score); (3) MatchBeats' own count of completed non-tiebreak games equals the truth; (4) no independent record holding the match reads the row or names another first server; (5) with the candidate's tables, the swap changes only the row's two service-game counts, exchanged, which then equal the truth, and the row passes Stage 0's checks.
SVX.reasons: The first server is proven, and the record that proves it names servers correctly: on every match Court Vision holds (762, RG 2019-2024) and every match a hand chart holds (456, RG 2019-2026 and AO 2025) the record's first server equals MatchBeats'. The truth is right: on the matches whose row already equals it, the records read that same count (Court Vision 689, the charts 399; the other readings are retirements, where they count the unfinished game for its server); MatchBeats' own count of completed non-tiebreak games equals the truth on all 323 proposed swaps (302 files holding every point, and 21 AO files missing some points but holding every game; on all 455 AO 2025 matches classed equal or swapped). The rows are swapped, not otherwise wrong: where an independent record holds the match (69 of the 323: Court Vision 52, in RG 2019 13, 2020 13, 2021 26; the charts 25, in AO 2025 11, RG 2019 2, 2020 6, 2021 6; 8 by both), it reads the truth 69 times and the row never. In 270 the row is the score as if the winner had served first when the loser did, in 53 the exchange runs the other way. The box itself is the right way round: on the 302 whole files MatchBeats' serve points equal the row's for each named player, and RG's 2019-2021 rows equal RG's statistics on all eight counts, so only the two service-game counts are exchanged, not the names. Two RG 2019 rows (Halep d. Tsurenko, Halep d. Swiatek) fail Stage 0's B8 as recorded, the loser conceding more breaks than the service games the row gives her, and pass with the exchange. Tiebreak sets (97 swaps), long advantage final sets (6) and retirements (6) are handled the same way and agree with MatchBeats' completed games. The fix is clear, unique and correct: exchanging the two counts gives exactly the truth for both players in all 323, leaves the total (so B5) unchanged, and touches nothing else; no swap row is named by another box correction of the candidate (the combined table applies without a row named twice), and the one swapped RG 2023 match is left to its override, which already carries the truth. Links: AO 2025 files placed by tour, draw, round and both names (79 exact, 2 transliterations: Khumoun/Khumoyun Sultanov, Georgia/Giorgia Pedone); RG files by my round-2 link.

SVS.scope: All 558 proposed sets (sets_scope.csv, with my values, equal to the proposal's in all 558): 460 fills (RG 2013 and 2014, 167 each, service games blank beside serve points; RG 2017, 126 recorded as 0 and 0) and 98 others (AO 2019-2026 55; RG 2015 8, 2016 3, 2017 6, 2018 6, 2019 7, 2020 4, 2021 7, 2023 1, 2024 1); set_svgms on Sackmann's row. Bar: the 8 Oct bar. Tests per match: the first server proven by the file under my stricter test (557), or, for Pironkova d. Beck (RG 2014), whose file splits one game into two records of the same server, by the merged alternation with the row's own break points rejecting the other first server; my truth equal to the proposal's values; the operation's guards holding on the current rows; the truth passing the break-point identity for both players; no record against; and Stage 0's checks passing afterwards.
SVS.reasons: Every value is mine: the score's alternation from the first server MatchBeats proves, a tiebreak taking its turn uncounted and a retirement's score holding only finished games. MatchBeats' own completed games equal it on 557 of the 558; on Pironkova d. Beck its raw count is one higher only because the split game counts twice. The row's own break points confirm the first server independently of MatchBeats: in all 300 sets where the other first server would give other counts, the identity (games won outside tiebreaks = service games - breaks conceded + breaks made) rejects it, and the truth passes the identity in all 558. The independent records agree wherever they hold a match: Court Vision 33 and the hand charts 39, all reading the truth and naming the same first server. The fills are missing counts by the row's own showing: blanks or 0 and 0 beside serve points, which Stage 0 already treats as missing. The others are real errors, not another convention. None counts tiebreak games. 90 give both players the same count where the score forces different ones (one of them also a game short). The other 8 of RG 2015 move one game between the players, which the alternation rules out. Struff d. Tiafoe (RG 2020) has 26 and 25 where both tiebreaks fall on Struff's turns (truth 24 and 27). Every other fails the identity with the row's own break points. The fix: on the candidate as it stands (809 swaps included), only the 558 rows change, only in their two service-game counts, to the truth; every changed row of the whole frame is named by a table; the guards hold; B5 failures fall from 12 to 11 and B8 stays 0; no row loses a box. The sets bring back 455 boxes from 'service games missing' to full (RG 2013 164, RG 2014 164, RG 2017 126, RG 2023 1). Six RG 2013-2014 fills stay partial because those rows lack double faults too; their service games are still right, and the set is harmless.
